newsitem.title: USA: Man charged with running computer investment scheme.
newsitem.headline: Man charged with running computer investment scheme.

text.p: A Princeton, N.J., man has been indicted for allegedly running a fraudulent scheme to solicit investments over the America Online Inc. computer online service, federal prosecutors said Thursday.
A Manhattan federal jury named Sev Bajrami, 29, in a one-count mail fraud indictment.

Under the scheme, which began in June 1996, Bajrami posted numerous messages on the America Online computer network system using the screen named "FinTrd." The messages claimed that Bajrami had developed a successful, proprietary trading system for trading futures contracts for the Standard & Poors 500 Index, prosecutors charged.

Bajrami named his system "High-Impact" and posted messages on America Online that reflected, among other things, the results of profitable trades he had purportedly achieved through his "High-Impact" system.

He allegedly posted other messages on the America Online network soliciting investors for Jeta Financials Inc., which he said managed certain commodity futures trading pools using the "High Impact" system, prosecutors said.
According to the indictment, Jeta was not a registered commodity pool operator and had never conducted any trading activity in any of the identified commodity pool accounts.
